incompatibleNotice.contradictionNote: The list says the extension is there and the object says it is not. That is not a weaker disguise — it is a self-contradiction, and it costs a detector two calls with no permission, no timing and no reference device. Anti-fraud systems check exactly this pair, because it is the cheapest way to catch a rewritten extension list.

settings.api.help: Local HTTP API (axum) for scripting — create/launch/close profiles and get a CDP WebSocket URL. Binds *127.0.0.1* only, JWT Bearer auth. Changes to enable/port apply after restarting the app.
settings.api.title: Automation API
settings.args.help:
Appended to every profile launch, one per line or space-separated. They go on *last*, so a switch repeated here is the one the engine sees — which is also how you get to undo one of the launcher's own. Quote a value with spaces.
Anything that changes what a page can measure belongs in the profile, not here: a switch applied to every profile at once makes them all alike, which is the opposite of what a profile is for.
settings.args.title: Extra launch arguments
settings.camera.help: The profile gets ShardX's camera instead of the machine's, and shows the picture or clip you pick from the control left of the browser's app menu. *Leave this on.* The profile's fingerprint already names a particular camera, so handing a page the host's real one contradicts the profile and identifies the machine behind every profile on it.

settings.helper.help:
Watches each page for fields a generated identity fits — names, email, phone, date of birth — and offers to fill them. It only ever *offers*: nothing is typed until you press the button on the panel that appears. Values come from the profile's own language, and go in through the same human typing the rest of the browser uses.
*Never runs on a synchronised launch.* In a group whatever you type in one window is mirrored into the others already, so a helper per window would find the same form ten times and offer ten prompts for one page.
settings.helper.title: Shard Helper
settings.helper.triggersHelp: Nothing selected means every kind. Narrow it if the panel appears on forms you do not care about — a login page with an email field is still a form.

settings.startShardxLauncherWhenYouSignI: Start ShardX Launcher when you sign in so its embedded Automation API is ready without opening the window. The MCP server remains a lightweight stdio process started on demand by Codex or another MCP client; it does not need a separate always-on daemon.

settings.whatsNew.help: After an update the launcher opens the patch log once, so the changes get seen before they surprise anyone. This reopens it on demand — useful when that first run went by in a hurry, or when someone else installed the update on this machine.
